# origincloud_dns_record_set (Resource)

Every record of one name and type in a hosted zone.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "origincloud_dns_hosted_zone" "example" {
  project    = "my-project-123"
  dns_name   = "example.com"
  visibility = "PUBLIC"
}

# Values of its own.
resource "origincloud_dns_record_set" "www" {
  project     = "my-project-123"
  hosted_zone = basename(origincloud_dns_hosted_zone.example.name)
  dns_name    = "www.example.com"
  type        = "A"
  ttl         = "60s"
  basic       = { values = ["192.0.2.10", "192.0.2.11"] }
}

resource "origincloud_dns_record_set" "mail" {
  project     = "my-project-123"
  hosted_zone = basename(origincloud_dns_hosted_zone.example.name)
  dns_name    = "example.com"
  type        = "MX"
  ttl         = "3600s"
  basic       = { values = ["10 mail.example.com"] }
}

# An alias: the record set answers with the floating IP's address, and
# follows it as it changes. An alias is of type A.
resource "origincloud_network_floating_ip" "web" {
  project = "my-project-123"
  zone    = "eu-central1-az1"
}

resource "origincloud_dns_record_set" "apex" {
  project     = "my-project-123"
  hosted_zone = basename(origincloud_dns_hosted_zone.example.name)
  dns_name    = "example.com"
  type        = "A"
  ttl         = "300s"
  alias       = { floating_ip = origincloud_network_floating_ip.web.name }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `dns_name` (String) The name the records answer for: the zone's `dns_name` or a name below it, written in full, such as `www.example.com`, without the final dot; answered in lowercase. Labels may hold `_` (`_dmarc.example.com`), and `*` only as the whole leftmost label, for a wildcard. Changing it replaces the record set, unless it is the same name in another case.
- `hosted_zone` (String) The hosted zone the record set is in. Changing it replaces the record set.
- `project` (String) The project the record set is in. Changing it replaces the record set.
- `type` (String) The records' type. An alias is `A`. One of `A`, `AAAA`, `CNAME`, `TXT`, `MX`, `SRV`, `CAA`. Changing it replaces the record set.

### Optional

- `alias` (Attributes) The address of a platform resource, followed as it changes. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--alias))
- `basic` (Attributes) Values of its own. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--basic))
- `ttl` (String) How long resolvers may keep the answer, from 30 seconds to 7 days, in whole seconds. 300 seconds when left out. A duration in seconds, such as `90s` or `1.5s`. Left out, it keeps its current value; see the field's description.

### Read-Only

- `create_time` (String) When the record set was created. An RFC 3339 timestamp, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`.
- `id` (String) The record set's resource name, the same as `name`.
- `name` (String) The record set's resource name.
- `update_time` (String) When the record set was last changed. An RFC 3339 timestamp, such as `2026-11-01T12:00:00Z`.
- `urn` (String) The record set's URN, the identifier access policies and the audit log use.

<a id="nestedatt--alias"></a>
### Nested Schema for `alias`

Required:

- `floating_ip` (String) The Floating IP whose address the record set answers with, in the zone's project. A Floating IP's address is an IPv4 address, so the record set is of type `A`; an `AAAA` alias is refused.


<a id="nestedatt--basic"></a>
### Nested Schema for `basic`

Required:

- `values` (Set of String) The records' values, 1 to 100, each once, written as `type` says. Names are written in full without the final dot, and answered in lowercase. - `A`: an IPv4 address, `192.0.2.10`. - `AAAA`: an IPv6 address, `2001:db8::10`. - `CNAME`: one name, `www.example.net`. - `TXT`: the text as it is, printable ASCII, up to 4000 characters, without quotes; it is split into strings of 255 characters on the wire. - `MX`: `{preference} {exchange}`, `10 mail.example.com`. `0 .`, alone, says the name takes no mail. - `SRV`: `{priority} {weight} {port} {target}`, `10 5 5060 sip.example.com`. A target of `.`, alone, says the service isn't offered. - `CAA`: `{flags} {tag} {value}`, `0 issue letsencrypt.org`: flags 0 or 128, the value as it is, without quotes.

A record set's records take at most 16 KiB on the wire.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A record set is imported by its resource name.
terraform import origincloud_dns_record_set.www projects/my-project-123/hostedZones/hz-XEkE66gA3ma/recordSets/rrset-XGFinQHdETZ
```
